name: Starter: Chinese (Traditional)
about: Traditional Chinese and everyday Taiwan Mandarin: when and where before the verb, Taiwan words such as 捷運 and 公車, and the little words that make questions and the past.

words.很: very; often just makes a plain adjective statement
words.有: to have; there is; (Taiwan speech) did, have done
words.在: to be at or in; at, in; (doing) now
words.打電話: to make a phone call, to call
words.呢: (marks a follow-up: what about …? where is …?)
words.著: (after a verb) marks an ongoing state

xiexie.about: Thanks to someone; 謝謝 alone says it too.

concept.line: In a simple action sentence, the subject comes before the verb and its object after it: 我喝茶, I drink tea.

words.means: very; often an unstressed degree marker before an adjective

concept.line: 嗎 at the end makes a yes/no question; the order stays the same.

words.means: to be (linking the subject to a noun or noun phrase)

concept.line: 是 joins two nouns: 我是學生, I'm a student.
的 joins a describer or an owner to a noun: 我的書, my book.
A number, 這 or 幾 takes a measure word before the noun: 一個人, one person; 兩張票, two tickets; 這個, this one.
在 with a place goes before the verb it happens at: 我在家吃飯, I eat at home.
